concerns.message: Acceptance 6's sweep (every 8 heading units × start speeds 0/half/full × lateral offsets 'across the reach', each must moor and never ground outside the reach) is partly infeasible under the mandated rule 'brake at the braking rate while a berth is in reach'. With shipTuning (maxSpeed 39, braking 3, dockMaxSpeed 15, dockRadius 384, SUB_UNITS_PER_TILE≈256), braking from 39 to ≤15 takes 8 steps and ~204 sub-units of travel (36+33+…+15), plus up to 39 of entry depth. A full-speed path whose chord through the 384 reach is shorter than ~243 (lateral offset ≳364), or an angled heading that carries the ship sideways out of the reach before it reaches the coast, leaves the reach still above dockMaxSpeed. Braking stops there, held ahead re-accelerates the ship, and it can run aground outside the reach. step.ts:52-57 only brakes/moors while dockInReach finds a berth, so nothing carries the braking past the reach edge.
concerns.consequence: The worker must either fail the sweep, quietly narrow the offset/heading domain (an acceptance change that reviewers flag, which is how sea-compact-001 got blocked), raise braking/dockRadius (breaks the ±25 % handling tests against the new literal baseline), or stop with `question` mid-run. The operator should fix the sweep domain now: e.g. start outside the reach on a line aimed within ±(dockRadius − fullSpeedBrakeDistance − maxSpeed) of the berth centre, with headings limited to those that point into the berth's open sides, and the bound computed from shipTuning in the test.

concerns.message: Acceptance 7 needs the simulation to tell a server lapse apart from a real neutral input. `PlayerInput`/`NEUTRAL_INPUT` live in packages/simulation/src/input.ts, and neither that file nor packages/simulation/src/index.ts is an owned path. The owned-path route is: MatchRoom/InputGate (apps) omit the entry (or pass undefined) for a lapsed gate, and step.ts treats a missing StepInputs entry as 'no fresh input: keep a moored ship's mooredThrottle'. That changes the documented meaning of 'a ship without an entry is neutral' (step.ts:8), which should be updated.
concerns.consequence: A worker who adds a `lapsed` field to PlayerInput touches an unowned path and must report `blocked` under the Stop rules, wasting the run.

concerns.message: The stall test in acceptance 7 can pass without the fix. step.ts:47 keeps a moored ship put whenever interact is held. If the test resumes after the 400 ms stall with ahead AND E held, the ship stays moored even with today's latch reset. Today the bug shows only once E is released while ahead stays held (direction 1 ≠ reset latch 0).
concerns.consequence: A test that resumes with E held proves nothing, and the regression could come back unnoticed. The test must resume with ahead held and E released (or release E after resuming) and assert the ship is still moored.

concerns.message: Web unit tests run with environment 'node' (vitest.config.ts:18) on a bare `new EventTarget()`. No jsdom/happy-dom is installed (they appear only as optional peers in package-lock). Dispatching a real keydown reaches keyboard.ts:39 `isTyping`, which evaluates `target instanceof HTMLInputElement`, a ReferenceError in Node. vitest.config.ts and package-lock.json are not owned.
concerns.consequence: The tap test from acceptance 3 errors out, or reports an unhandled error, unless the worker stubs the HTMLInputElement/HTMLTextAreaElement globals in the test (vi.stubGlobal) or makes isTyping safe when those globals are missing. Trying to add a DOM environment hits unowned files.

concerns.message: assets/source/maps/sketch.ts writes slice-sea.tmj as a side effect at import (lines 213-214, writeFileSync), and imports node:fs. packages/content/tsconfig.json has `types: []`, so a maps.test.ts import of sketch.ts pulls node:fs into the content package's typecheck.
concerns.consequence: Importing it as-is overwrites the committed map during `npm run test:unit`, which makes the drift test unreliable and dirties the checkout, and the typecheck may fail. The generator must be split into a pure exported function (no fs) plus a small entry script that writes the file, keeping the documented `node assets/source/maps/sketch.ts` command working.

concerns.message: Acceptance 2 lists seven baseline values, but ShipTuning also needs maxReverseSpeed (16), reverseAcceleration (2), turnRate and hullHalfSize. Today these are inherited by spreading config.ship (simulation.test.ts:288). A literal baseline must name all of them, and turnRate matters because the test asserts equal 3.2 s turn times.
concerns.consequence: If the worker guesses the missing pre-compact values or spreads them from the current config, the baseline again partly tracks the current config, which is the exact flaw acceptance 2 is meant to fix. The values should be taken from the pre-compact commit's sailing.ts.

structured_output.simpler_alternative: For docking (item 6): when interact is held and dockInReach finds a berth with a clear hull path, moor at any speed, dropping the dockMaxSpeed gate inside the reach. Mooring already snaps the ship up to 1.5 tiles to the berth centre, so a snap at speed matches how docking already looks. It adds no new braking state and has no reach-edge failures, so every heading/offset/speed case in the sweep moors in one step. For the stall (item 7): leave PlayerInput alone. MatchRoom omits the StepInputs entry for a gate whose held input has lapsed (and has no latched buttons), and step.ts keeps a moored ship's mooredThrottle when its entry is missing. The change stays within step.ts and apps/server, with no protocol or input.ts change.
structured_output.cheap_experiment: Before any worker starts, add a throwaway vitest to simulation.test.ts that uses the existing testConfig/shipAt/sailFor helpers. Build a small harbour with one dock, apply the proposed 'brake at braking rate while E is held in reach' rule (a local copy of sail with the extra branch is enough), and sweep full-speed starts across lateral offsets 0..384 in steps of 16 and headings every 8 units. Record which cases moor and which leave the reach or ground outside it. This takes about 15 minutes. It shows whether the acceptance-6 sweep can pass as written, and gives the exact offset/heading bound to write into the acceptance or a reason to switch to moor-at-any-speed.
